The proposed safeguard is **to develop model-transfer procedures and guidelines and tailor transferred models to the local population**, rather than reuse them unchanged. This addresses differences in demographics, behavior, cultural norms, and data collection that may affect how well a model captures the virus’s spread and effects. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.09043)

A concrete, general transfer-learning mechanism is **TrAdaBoost**: it combines source-population data with a few labeled examples from the target population, then iteratively reweights the source examples so that harmful examples contribute less and useful ones contribute more. Training uses weighted source and target data, but error is calculated only on target data, making the adaptation target-focused. The method assumes the same features and labels across populations, despite different data distributions. Another proposed method removes “misleading” source examples based on differences between source and target conditional probabilities. These are general transfer-learning proposals, not pandemic-specific forecasting results in the passage. (https://www.cse.ust.hk/~qyang/Docs/2009/tkde_transfer_learning.pdf)
